engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to identify and capture cost savings across key spend areas, establish stronger procurement processes/controls, and ultimately increase enterprise value by delivering an estimated $730K–$1.4M in annual savings from strategic sourcing.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Project covers 10 spend categories representing about $18.98 M in annual spend (≈$45 M total company spend, of which ~$19 M is addressable). In-scope categories: Employee Benefits (optional timing), Medical Devices-IUDs, Diagnostic Devices & Services, Billing Systems/RCM, Medical Supplies, Medical Equipment, Telecom–Data & Voice, Electronic Payment Processing, Data Center/Cloud Hosting, and Office Supplies. Activities include RFPs, incumbent negotiations, and GPO leverage; some spend may later be deemed non-addressable after deep-dive analysis.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus prior to the project
Spend data split between two AP/P-card systems (Advantia Mid-Atlantic and Heartland) with inconsistent item-level detail
Ongoing acquisition integration gaps causing decentralized, fragmented supplier base
Difficulty obtaining detailed usage data from certain high-spend suppliers, leading to potential data gaps
Tight project timeline of ~6 months for most categories with separate July–Oct window for Benefits workstream
Need to avoid parallel procurement activities by the client to prevent mixed signals in the supplier marketplace

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP data (Oct 2020–Sep 2021) and YTD P-card data were available; contracts scattered; line-item usage data had to be requested from suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple vendor naming conventions, two separate accounting systems, limited item-level visibility, and non-responsive suppliers caused data completeness issues.
